why: The minimum cost to reach the end with a small state: keep the cheapest total so far ending in each of the three colors; each house adds its color cost to the cheaper of the other two colors.
hints: After painting house i, what do you need to remember to decide house i+1? Only the color of house i matters.
best[c] for house i = costs[i][c] + min(best of the other two colors for house i-1).
Keep three variables and roll them; the answer is the min of the three after the last house. O(n).
pitfalls: Picking the cheapest color per house greedily can force an expensive neighbour.
One house: return its cheapest color.
